problem.text: Using the diagram below and the concept that you just learned, find the measures of angles $a$, $b$, and $c$.

steps.title: Where to start: each line is a straight angle
steps.body: The only number given is $47^\circ$, and the diagram is just two straight lines crossing. A straight line makes an angle of $180^\circ$, so two angles that sit side by side along the same line add up to $180^\circ$. Start by finding which of $a$, $b$, $c$ sit right next to the $47^\circ$ angle.

your_turn.prompt: Which of the angles $a$, $b$, $c$ share a side with the $47^\circ$ angle?
your_turn.answer: $a$ and $c$. Angle $a$ is on the other side of the upward ray, and $c$ is on the other side of the upper-left ray.

steps.title: Write the straight-line equations
steps.body:
The $47^\circ$ angle and $c$ together fill the angle from the upward ray to the downward ray, which is the nearly vertical line. The $47^\circ$ angle and $a$ together fill the angle from the upper-left ray to the lower-right ray, which is the other line.
$$47 + c = 180, \qquad 47 + a = 180$$

your_turn.prompt: Without computing anything, explain why $a$ and $c$ must be equal.
your_turn.answer: Both are $180$ minus the same angle, $47^\circ$.

steps.title: Bring in angle $b$
steps.body: Angle $b$ is not next to the $47^\circ$ angle; it is across from it. But $b$ does sit next to $a$ and next to $c$, so it is tied to them by a straight line as well.

your_turn.prompt: Write one straight-line equation that links $a$ and $b$.
your_turn.answer: $a + b = 180$, because $a$ and $b$ together go from the upward ray to the downward ray.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: From $47 + c = 180$ we get $c = 133^\circ$, and in the same way $a = 133^\circ$. Then $a + b = 180$ gives $b = 180 - 133 = 47^\circ$. Notice that the angles across from each other came out equal ($b$ matches $47^\circ$ and $a$ matches $c$); this is the vertical angle theorem. The answer is **$a = 133^\circ$, $b = 47^\circ$, $c = 133^\circ$**.
